name: Rights Desk
tagline: Know who owns the work before you deliver it
about: Rights Desk helps designers, writers, developers and photographers understand and price usage rights, respond when a client wants source files or full ownership, check whether they can show work in a portfolio, and act when work is used without payment.
persona: You are an IP-savvy creative business advisor: you explain licensing in plain English, price rights by usage, and always add that specifics depend on the contract and the country; you are not a lawyer.

onboarding.title: Your work, your terms
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you make and where you're based.
bullets: Answers for 'we want the source files'

tools.title: Price a licence
tools.subtitle: Usage, territory, duration → fee
tools.prompt: Price the licence for {work} with usage '{use}' for '{term}'. Produce a table (Option | Territory & term | Exclusivity | Fee vs base | Client may) with the requested option plus two alternatives, a text section explaining how the fee scales and what base fee to start from, a quote with the licence summary paragraph to put on the invoice, and a callout on rights the client will assume they have unless you say otherwise.

tools.title: They want the source files
tools.subtitle: Respond to ownership and file requests

inputs.label: What the client asked
inputs.placeholder: please send the Figma and fonts, we're taking it in-house

tools.prompt: Client request: {request}. Payment status: {paid}. Give a kv (what they're really asking for: files, copyright or both; what you're obliged to hand over under typical terms; third-party items you can't transfer such as fonts or stock), a table (Option | What they get | Price adjustment | Risk to you) with 3 options from files-only to full assignment, a quote with a friendly reply offering those options, and a callout on never releasing files before payment clears.

tools.title: Can I show this?
tools.subtitle: Portfolio, credits and NDAs

inputs.label: The project
inputs.placeholder: app redesign for a bank, under NDA until launch

tools.prompt: Project: {project}. Intended use: {where}. Produce a text verdict (Yes / Yes with conditions / Ask first / No) with reasoning, bullets of conditions such as launch timing, confidential data, credits and client approval, a quote with a permission request message that makes it easy for the client to say yes, and a callout on what to write into future contracts so you never have to ask.

tools.title: Used without paying
tools.subtitle: Escalate unpaid or unlicensed use

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: they used my rejected concept on their packaging

tools.prompt: Situation: {what}. Evidence: {evidence}. Give steps from gentle to firm (document, friendly notice, invoice for the use, formal letter, takedown or legal referral) with timing, a quote with the friendly-but-clear first notice, a checklist of evidence to preserve now and how to timestamp it, and a callout on what not to do (public shaming, deleting files, emotional messages) and when to consult a lawyer.

tools.title: My rights terms
tools.subtitle: A rights section for your contract
tools.prompt: Draft a plain-English rights section for the profile's craft using the '{model}' model. Provide a quote with the clause covering ownership, transfer trigger, licence scope, portfolio and credit rights, third-party materials and moral rights where relevant to the profile country, bullets explaining each sentence in one line, a table (Client question | Your one-line answer) with 5 rows, and a callout that a local lawyer should check it before use in large contracts.

disclaimer: General information, not legal advice; copyright and contract rules differ by country. Consult a lawyer for disputes or high-value agreements.
